claim_verdicts.evidence: CertificateRevocationListBuilder.Build (net-10.0): issuerCertificate "The certificate representing the Certificate Authority (CA) that is creating this Certificate Revocation List"; nextUpdate "The latest possible time before the CA will publish a newer CRL"; Returns "the bytes of the signed CRL". Signed by the CA, published at intervals; a signed byte array can be fetched and kept.

Round 3: text unchanged; round 2 notes say it stays unverified. Round 2: versions.yaml has no OCSP/RFC 6960 key (grep 'ocsp|6960': no match). Round 1: refs/ grep finds only mentions (cross-platform-cryptography.md, aspnetcore linux-nginx.md OCSP stapling), no statement that a responder returns a signed answer about one certificate; rfc8446 only mentions OCSP. Kind behavior: not blocking.

Rfc3161TimestampRequest.CreateFromHash (net-10.0): "Create a timestamp request using a pre-computed hash value"; parameters are hash, hashAlgorithm, requestedPolicyId, nonce, requestSignerCertificates, extensions: no time parameter, so the requester does not set the time. Rfc3161TimestampTokenInfo.IsOrdering remark: "Timestamp indicates when the token has been created by the TSA".

ADR 0029 lines 40-41: "chỉ gửi hash, không gửi bảng kê". Rfc3161TimestampRequest.CreateFromHash: "Create a timestamp request using a pre-computed hash value" - the request carries a hash, not the document.

issues.text: Carried from round 2 (originally round 1). Claim 2 (OCSP: ask a responder about one certificate, get a signed answer) is unverified: RFC 6960 is not a docs root in versions.yaml and the allowed .NET/ASP.NET/RFC 8446 pages only mention OCSP. Kind behavior, so not blocking.
issues.quote: OCSP (Online Certificate Status Protocol) — a way for a verifier to ask the CA's responder about one certificate and get a signed answer about its status.
issues.fix: No lesson text change required. Owner may add a standards key for OCSP (RFC 6960) to content/versions.yaml so a re-review can verify claim 2; otherwise keep it as unverified behavior.

issues.quote: The timestamp is itself signed by the TSA, and the TSA's certificate ends too; the review has the package timestamped again before then, as a recurring job.
issues.text: Carried from round 2. 'that certificate' is now clearly the TSA's, so the why is fine. Still not said how a new stamp keeps the old one checkable: section 4 says a timestamp covers the signature's hash, so I do not know what the new stamp covers or why it rescues the old one. Minor: the main idea does not depend on it.
issues.fix: If the repo supports it, add one clause after 'as a recurring job': what the new timestamp is taken over (e.g. the package with its old timestamp). If the repo is silent, leave as is.

issues.quote: Its decision picks the second of its four options; the first, the server's time and Đơn Hàng's own root, is rejected, as are the other two.
issues.text: New in the changed sentence. I learn there are four options and the first is named, but 'the other two' are never named anywhere in the lesson, so I stop and wonder what they were. Not needed for the main idea.
issues.fix: Either name the other two in a few words each (e.g. 'Đơn Hàng's own HSM, and sharing the invoice key') or drop the count: 'Its decision picks the second option; the first, the server's time and Đơn Hàng's own root, is rejected.'

issues.quote: The next lesson weighs both costs.
issues.text: New in the changed paragraph. I had to re-read to find which two costs: statements waiting when a service fails, and the recurring re-timestamp job. 'both' is far from what it points to.
issues.fix: Name them: 'The next lesson weighs both costs: statements waiting on three services, and the re-timestamp job.'
